o.text: From Proto-Common Turkic *tirs-gek, a derivation from Proto-Turkic *tīŕ, whence also Azerbaijani diz (“knee”).

From yalın (“bare, naked”) remodeled after göyərçin (“dove; dove-coloured”) and sarışın (“yellowish, blond”), where the suffix -çin/-şın signifies color nuances. Possibly a borrowing from Ottoman Turkish يالچين (yalçın, “smooth and bare”).
From Proto-Turkic *ēn-. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (en-, “to go down”), Turkish and Turkmen inmek, and Chuvash ан (an).
From earlier *uğuramaq, ultimately from Proto-Common Turkic *ugur, whence also Azerbaijani uğur.
